findings.claim: No test would fail if findAdmissionClosedWithReads lost its StopFence skip: T2 checks the fenced goal only at the grace boundary, which is already outside the closed band, and T1's stops are fakes that write no fence.
findings.evidence: TestFindAdmissionClosedListsOnlyTheClosedBand calls bed.stop("bounded", 2, boundary) and then bed.spent(boundary); at boundary the projection is past the band, so the list is empty either way. In spent_box_test.go every BreachStop is a fake that returns "stopped" and fences nothing.
findings.change: Later list: check a fenced goal at the in-band clock (between), so that dropping the skip fails the test.

findings.claim: The channel status report's Needs-you line says 'decide whether to resume it.' for every open question of kind stop, so the spent-box question (kind stop under S6) reads as a resume for a goal that is not stopped.
findings.evidence: internal/channel/report.go:100 builds 'Needs you: '+featureName(q.Goal)+' — '+questionRequest(q); questionRequest maps case "stop" to 'decide whether to resume it.' (report.go:286). The question's own thread carries the right words.
findings.change: Later list: let questionRequest read Decision.Kind budget-admission (or the contract question's Plain.Decision) before the kind fallback.

findings.claim: For each spent box on this machine, the built-work evidence (the unit reader, git worktree list and git status --porcelain) is read on every tick, even while the question is already open, because spentBoxAsk is built before AskOrFind finds the open question.
findings.evidence: signal_channel.go askSpentBoxes: channel.AskOrFind(spentBoxAsk(repoRoot, box, builtWorkWaiting(repoRoot, cfg, box.GoalID), now)) runs for every listed box on every tick; build brief step 4e prescribes this exact call shape.
findings.change: None required; if it shows in tick timing, read the evidence only when no open question holds the box's state.
findings.relation: builder rule 3 (reads only for a box this machine asks about): complies; cost only
